name: PRAKASH AMRITRAJ
bio:
Career Overview: Playing Style: An aggressive player with a strong serve and solid baseline game, effective on hard courts.
Career-High ATP Singles Ranking: #154 (October 15, 2007), Career-High ATP Doubles Ranking: #119 (October 26, 2009).
Best Grand Slam Singles Performance: Reached the second round of Wimbledon qualifying (2002, 2006); never qualified for a Grand Slam main draw.
Notable Achievements: ATP Finals: Reached the 2006 Newport final (lost to Mark Philippoussis), his only ATP singles final. Challenger Success: Won 2 ATP Challenger singles titles (2006 Tumkur, 2008 New Delhi) and 2 doubles titles. Davis Cup & National Representation: Represented India in Davis Cup ties from 2003 to 2008, with a 5-5 singles record, including a win over Rik de Voest (2008).
Other Highlights: Son of tennis legend Vijay Amritraj, continuing the family legacy. Played college tennis at USC before turning pro. Transitioned to a career as a broadcaster and commentator for Tennis Channel post-retirement.
Prakash retired in 2010, leaving a mark as a bridge between India’s golden era and modern players. 🎾🇮🇳
